source.title: Resolution of Some Open Problems Concerning Multiple Zeta Evaluations of Arbitrary Depth

accepted.question_text: For each positive integer k, let Z_k denote the set of all multiple zeta values with positive integer arguments and depth less than k. Given positive integers s_1, …, s_k with s_1 > 1 so that ζ(s_1, …, s_k) converges, determine for which k-tuples (s_1, …, s_k) the depth-k multiple zeta value ζ(s_1, …, s_k) lies in the polynomial ring Q[Z_k], meaning that it can be expressed by a rational polynomial relation in multiple zeta values of smaller depth.
accepted.context_brief: General depth-reduction problem for multiple zeta values

evidence.quote: For each positive integer k, let Zk denote the set of all multiple zeta values (with positive integer arguments) of depth less than k. If we restrict our attention to rational polynomial relationships, the aforementioned problem amounts to determining for each k the values of the arguments s1; ... ;sk for which the sum (1) lies in the polynomial ring Q[Zk]. Settling this question in complete generality is currently well beyond the reach of number theory.

accepted.question_text: Is the Riemann zeta value ζ(5) irrational; equivalently, does ζ(5) fail to lie in Q[Z_1] = Q?

evidence.quote: For example, there is as yet no proof that z(5) ∉ Q[Z1] = Q, although it is strongly suspected that z(5) is indeed irrational.

accepted.question_text: For every nonnegative integer n, does the multiple zeta value ζ(2, {1, 3}^n) satisfy the identity ζ(2, {1, 3}^n) = 4^{-n} Σ_{k=0}^{n} (-1)^k ζ({4}^{n-k}) {(4k + 1)ζ(4k + 2) - 4 Σ_{j=1}^{k} ζ(4j - 1)ζ(4k - 4j + 3)}, where {1, 3}^n denotes n repetitions of the pair (1, 3) and {4}^{n-k} denotes n-k repetitions of 4?

evidence.quote: THEOREM 2 (Conjectured in [4] and [5]). For all nonnegative integers n, z(2,{1, 3}^n) = 4^{-n}Σ_{k=0}^{n} (-1)^k z({4}^{n-k}) {(4k + 1)z(4k + 2) - 4 Σ_{j=1}^{k} z(4j - 1)z(4k - 4j + 3)}.
Other results we provide settle three of the remaining outstanding conjectures of Borwein, Bradley, and Broadhurst.

accepted.question_text: Let A(z) = Σ_{n=0}^{∞} z^n ζ({̅1}^n), using the alternating Euler-sum notation of the source. For every complex number t, does the generating function identity Σ_{n=0}^{∞} [t^{2n} ζ({̅1, 1}^n) + t^{2n+1} ζ(̅1, {̅1, 1}^n)] = A(t/(1-i)) A(t/(1+i)) hold?
accepted.context_brief: Conjectured generating function for alternating unit Euler sums

evidence.quote: COROLLARY 1 (Conjectured in [4]). Let A(z) be as in (12). Then for all complex numbers t, we have Σ [t^{2n} z({1, 1}^n) + t^{2n+1} z(1,{1, 1}^n)] = A(t/(1 - i)) A(t/(1 + i)).
Other results we provide settle three of the remaining outstanding conjectures of Borwein, Bradley, and Broadhurst.

accepted.question_text: Let G and A be the functions defined in equations (9) and (12), and let z = (1+i)t/2. Using the alternating Euler-sum notation of the source, does the identity 1 + Σ_{n=0}^{∞} [t^{2n+1} ζ(̅1, {̅1, 1}^n) + t^{2n+2} ζ(̅1, ̅1, {1, ̅1}^n)] = (1/2)(1+i) z A(z) A(-iz) {π csc(πz) - iπ csch(πz) + 4G(z)} hold whenever the right-hand side is defined?
accepted.context_brief: Second conjectured generating function for alternating unit Euler sums

evidence.quote: COROLLARY 2 [Conjectured in [4]). Let the functions G and A be given by (9) and (12), respectively. Then 1 + Σ [t^{2n+1} z(1,{1, 1}^n) + t^{2n+2} z(1, 1,{1, 1}^n)] = (1/2)(1 + i)zA(z)A(-iz){π csc(πz) - iπ csch(πz) + 4G(z)}, holds for all complex numbers t and z satisfying z = (1 + i)t/2 and such that the right-hand side is defined.
Other results we provide settle three of the remaining outstanding conjectures of Borwein, Bradley, and Broadhurst.
